key_facts: The Eurospeech paper was accepted and will be presented in Aalborg, Denmark, in September.
PhD C discussed experiments on online normalization, including varying time constants and using different means for silence and speech, but found no significant improvement.
Adding white noise at a level 15 dB below the peak energy of utterances made MFCCs smoother and did not worsen speech recognition performance.
PhD C mentioned that the LDA filter derived from clean speech improved recognition rates on TI-Digits from 82.7% to 85.1%.
Grad A plans to conduct experiments on phone recognition using TIMIT, incorporating knowledge of voicing to improve results.
Grad G mentioned that training a Broadcast News net takes two to three weeks, and scaling down the net can reduce training time by a quarter.
PhD D encountered issues with Wiener filtering, suspecting a bug in the implementation, and plans to try a modified approach using filters from Carlos' thesis.
PhD E is working on VTS for noise removal, using a single Gaussian for noise estimation and a codebook for clean speech, with plans to improve noise modeling.
Professor B suggested using known nonspeech sections for noise estimation to better understand the impact of different methods on performance.
PhD E explained the VTS method involves a Taylor series expansion to estimate the PDF of noisy speech based on statistics of clean and noisy speech.
PhD E mentioned that the noise estimation is done using only the first ten frames of an utterance and is fixed per utterance.
Professor B questioned whether using more parameters to characterize noise could improve performance, especially with better boundaries from VAD.
PhD E confirmed that only the first term of the vector Taylor series is used in the current implementation, and higher-order terms are complicated.
PhD F mentioned that some digit forms do not contain digits, and not everyone will be reading digits in the experiment.
